section_summary: A report analyzes Japan’s January 23, 1949 House of Representatives election, including party gains, campaign rules, Occupation surveillance, turnout, and election violations. It also describes the first popular review of Supreme Court judges under the new Constitution, with a sample ballot and results. The section ends with a largely illegible incoming telegram and the opening page of a despatch on factions within the Democratic Liberal Party.

subfiles.title: General Election of Members of the House of Representatives, January 23, 1949, and Referendum on the Judges of the Supreme Court
subfiles.doc_type: report with statistical tables, sample ballot, and electoral map
subfiles.about: Reports on the 1949 Japanese general election and the first popular review of Supreme Court judges.
subfiles.summary: The Democratic Liberal Party won an absolute majority of 264 of 466 House seats, while the Communists gained and most other parties lost seats. The report examines the dissolution of the preceding Diet, party platforms, campaign regulation and publicity, Occupation surveillance, turnout, representation, and election law violations, with comparative statistics and an electoral map. It explains the constitutional and statutory procedures for reviewing Supreme Court judges and records overwhelming votes to retain all fourteen judges.

subfiles.title: Incoming telegram, February 25, 1949

subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR reveals the telegram form, date, and filing number but no reliable message text.

subfiles.title: Factions Within Democratic Liberal Party
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese press commentary on emerging factions in the Democratic Liberal Party.
subfiles.summary: The opening page forwards an article and editorial from the Nippon Times and notes growing differences among party leaders after the January election.
